sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: You hear that?
sentences.zh: 你听到了吗？

sentences.en: One of the most beautiful sounds I heard.
sentences.zh: 我听过最美的声音之一。

sentences.en: I grew up mainly in Ohio, and in the 80s, I only knew about New York City from the movies.
sentences.zh: 我主要在俄亥俄州长大，在80年代，我对纽约市的全部了解都来自于电影。

sentences.en: And all the movies, every single one of them, had this one establishing shot that said,
sentences.zh: 所有的电影，无一例外，都有这样一个定场镜头，仿佛在告诉

sentences.en: audience, we are in New York City.
sentences.zh: 观众，我们身处纽约市。

sentences.en: It was a graffiti-covered subway.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆涂满涂鸦的地铁。

sentences.en: Oh, it's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 哦，太美了。

sentences.en: For me, a suburban kid from Ohio, that graffiti was exciting, but it didn't seem artistic or complicated.
sentences.zh: 对我这个来自俄亥俄州的郊区小孩来说，那些涂鸦令人兴奋，但它们看起来并不艺术，也不复杂。

sentences.en: It was just scary hooliganism.
sentences.zh: 那只是一种可怕的流氓行为。

sentences.en: Too bad you can't see.
sentences.zh: 真可惜你看不到。

sentences.en: The graffiti was a total mystery to me, too.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，涂鸦也是一个彻底的谜团。

sentences.en: Producer Ann Hepperman grew up in Nebraska, also far, far from New York City.
sentences.zh: 制片人安·赫珀曼在内布拉斯加州长大，同样远离纽约市。

sentences.en: It was like technicolor hieroglyphics.
sentences.zh: 它就像是彩色象形文字。

sentences.en: He doing the forward Z.
sentences.zh: 他在画正向的Z字。

sentences.en: Oh, he doing his s*** back to front.
sentences.zh: 哦，他把他的狗屎字反着写了。

sentences.en: All of these intersecting lines and colors, I mean, I knew that they were letters.
sentences.zh: 所有这些交织的线条和色彩，我的意思是，我知道它们是字母。

sentences.en: I just never knew what they said.
sentences.zh: 我只是从来不知道它们写的是什么。

sentences.en: New York was another planet, and graffiti was its language.
sentences.zh: 纽约是另一个星球，而涂鸦就是它的语言。

sentences.en: There's only 26 letters to the alphabet, but somehow, graffiti writers manipulate it, and they make it theirs.
sentences.zh: 字母表中只有26个字母，但不知何故，涂鸦创作者们操纵着它们，并打上了自己的印记。

sentences.en: And those trains looked so cool on the outside.
sentences.zh: 那些列车的外观看起来太酷了。

sentences.en: But the inside was a whole other story.
sentences.zh: 但车厢内部则是完全不同的另一回事。

sentences.en: You would not have gotten on that subway.
sentences.zh: 你根本不会想坐那趟地铁。

sentences.en: The place was filthy.
sentences.zh: 那个地方污秽不堪。

sentences.en: The trains smelled.
sentences.zh: 列车散发着异味。

sentences.en: They were dirty.
sentences.zh: 它们脏兮兮的。

sentences.en: The floor, you stuck to the floor.
sentences.zh: 地板，你的鞋子会被黏在地板上。

sentences.en: And you got stuck in the tunnels, and the cars filled up with smoke.
sentences.zh: 而且你会被困在隧道里，车厢里充满了烟雾。

sentences.en: And, I mean, it was a scary place to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一个可怕的地方。

sentences.en: In the 1970s and 80s, says this guy, David Gunn, the New York City subway was like some kind of daunting hellscape with fire and bloodshed and gangs.
sentences.zh: 据这位名叫大卫·冈恩的男子说，在20世纪70和80年代，纽约市地铁就像某种充满烈火、流血和帮派的令人畏惧的人间炼狱。

sentences.en: There was definitely a sense that, you know, the subways were totally controlled by wild gangs of teenagers.
sentences.zh: 当时确实有一种感觉，你知道，地铁完全被疯狂的青少年帮派控制了。

sentences.en: And they kind of were.
sentences.zh: 而且它们某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, all you boppers out there know that amongst the gangs, there were the rogues, the Gramercy Riffs, everyone's favorite, the Baseball Furies, and, of course, the Warriors.
sentences.zh: 现在，所有那些跳舞的小伙子们都知道，在各个帮派中，有恶棍帮、格拉梅西狂人帮，所有人最喜欢的棒球狂怒帮，当然，还有勇士帮。

sentences.en: I want you to hit everything in sight.
sentences.zh: 我要你们痛击视线内的所有东西。

sentences.en: I want everybody to know the Warriors were there.
sentences.zh: 我要让所有人都知道勇士帮来过。

sentences.en: Artist Caleb Nealon wields a mean spray can himself.
sentences.zh: 艺术家卡勒布·尼龙自己也是个喷漆好手。

sentences.en: But even he admits.
sentences.zh: 但连他也承认。

sentences.en: Graffiti was simply just this symbol that the city had lost control.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦根本只是这座城市失去控制的一个象征。

sentences.en: And it was a symbol that who knew what the future lay with cities.
sentences.zh: 这个象征表明，谁也不知道城市的未来会怎样。

sentences.en: It could be terrible.
sentences.zh: 可能会变得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And nothing pisses people off more than writing they can't read.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比他们看不懂的文字更能惹恼人们了。

sentences.en: So starting in the early 70s, the mayors of New York City vowed to eradicate graffiti.
sentences.zh: 因此，从70年代初开始，纽约市长们发誓要根除涂鸦。

sentences.en: First, Mayor John Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 首先是约翰·林赛市长。

sentences.en: He took office at really, like, one of the worst times for any New York mayor.
sentences.zh: 他上任时，确实是任何纽约市长面临的最糟糕时期之一。

sentences.en: Lindsay formed the first anti-graffiti task force.
sentences.zh: 林赛组成了第一个反涂鸦特别工作组。

sentences.en: And he turned graffiti from a nuisance.
sentences.zh: 他把涂鸦从一种讨厌的小事

sentences.en: Took it out of the category of littering or something like that.
sentences.zh: 将其从乱扔垃圾之类的范畴中抽离出来。

sentences.en: Into a crime.
sentences.zh: 变成了一种犯罪。

sentences.en: Into being, you know, a misdemeanor.
sentences.zh: 变成了一种轻罪。

sentences.en: But subway graffiti persisted.
sentences.zh: 但地铁涂鸦依然存在。

sentences.en: It was the problem that wouldn't go away.
sentences.zh: 这是一个挥之不去的问题。

sentences.en: For two decades, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, also known as the MTA, failed miserably trying to fix its graffiti problem.
sentences.zh: 二十年来，大都市交通管理局，也就是MTA，在试图解决涂鸦问题时彻底失败了。

sentences.en: Sometimes laughably.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至到了滑稽的地步。

sentences.en: Like the time they decided to repaint 7,000 subway cars all white.
sentences.zh: 比如他们决定把7000辆地铁车厢全部重新刷成白色的那一次。

sentences.en: They called it the Great White Fleet.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“伟大白色舰队”。

sentences.en: Oddly, what the graffiti movement needed at that time was new real estate.
sentences.zh: 说也奇怪，当时涂鸦运动最需要的是新的画布。

sentences.en: And then, before you knew it, you had the entire subway car covered in spray paint.
sentences.zh: 然后，不知不觉中，你就会发现整列地铁车厢都被喷漆覆盖了。

sentences.en: And then, there was Ed Koch's Berlin Wall method.
sentences.zh: 还有，埃德·科克的柏林墙方法。

sentences.en: Koch doubled up the fences in the yards.
sentences.zh: 科克在车场里加倍设置了围栏。

sentences.en: All of them topped with razor wire.
sentences.zh: 所有围栏顶端都装有刀片铁丝网。

sentences.en: Thus creating a no-man's land between them.
sentences.zh: 从而在它们之间创造了一个无人区。

sentences.en: Plus, attack dogs.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有攻击犬。

sentences.en: Here's Mayor Koch.
sentences.zh: 这是科克市长。

sentences.en: But I said, build two fences and have the dog run between the two fences.
sentences.zh: 但我说，建造两道围栏，让狗在两道围栏之间奔跑。

sentences.en: And that will keep people out and protect the dog from stepping on the third rail.
sentences.zh: 这样既能把人挡在外面，又能保护狗不会踩到第三轨触电。

sentences.en: And the response was, well, maybe somebody will climb over the fence and the dog will bite them.
sentences.zh: 当时的反应是，嗯，也许有人会翻过围栏，然后狗会咬他们。

sentences.en: I said, well, I thought that's what the dog was for.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我以为这正是养狗的目的。

sentences.en: And the razor wire topped fences and the German shepherds worked.
sentences.zh: 那些顶端有刀片铁丝网的围栏和德国牧羊犬起作用了。

sentences.en: Until the graffiti writers realized that they could distract the dogs with food and cut through the fences.
sentences.zh: 直到涂鸦者们意识到他们可以用食物分散狗的注意力，然后剪断围栏。

sentences.en: Desperate people take desperate measures.
sentences.zh: 走投无路的人会采取极端措施。

sentences.en: And the transit officials were desperate.
sentences.zh: 而交通官员们已经走投无路了。

sentences.en: No one knew what to do.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Until David Gunn.
sentences.zh: 直到大卫·冈恩出现。

sentences.en: I'm David Gunn.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·冈恩。

sentences.en: And I was president of the New York City Transit Authority for six years.
sentences.zh: 我曾担任纽约市交通局局长六年。

sentences.en: From 1984 to 1990.
If transit systems had halls of fame, David Gunn would be right up in front.
sentences.zh: 如果交通系统有名人堂，大卫·冈恩绝对位居前列。

sentences.en: David Gunn cleaned up subways in Boston, Philly, D.C.
sentences.zh: 大卫·冈恩清理过波士顿、费城、华盛顿特区

sentences.en: and Toronto.
sentences.zh: 和多伦多的地铁。

sentences.en: He headed up Amtrak for a while, too.
sentences.zh: 他还负责过一段时间的美国铁路客运公司。

sentences.en: He seemed invincible.
sentences.zh: 他似乎不可战胜。

sentences.en: But when it came to New York City in 1984.
sentences.zh: 但当他在1984年面对纽约市时。

sentences.en: My initial reaction was no, because it was, it just looked to be a hopeless situation.
sentences.zh: 我的最初反应是拒绝，因为这看起来是一个毫无希望的局面。

sentences.en: Gunn's actual words were suicide mission.
sentences.zh: 冈恩的原话是“自杀任务”。

sentences.en: But then his mother stepped in.
sentences.zh: 但随后他的母亲介入了。

sentences.en: At that point, she was in her 80s.
sentences.zh: 当时，她已经八十多岁了。

sentences.en: She said, you better take that or everybody will think you're a coward.
sentences.zh: 她说，你最好接下这个差事，否则每个人都会以为你是个懦夫。

sentences.en: MoMs.
sentences.zh: 妈妈们。

sentences.en: You gotta love MoMs.
sentences.zh: 你不能不爱妈妈们。

sentences.en: Gunn hit the ground running with something he called the Clean Train Program.
sentences.zh: 冈恩一上任就雷厉风行地推出了他所谓的“清洁列车计划”。

sentences.en: You know, everybody says you cleaned up the cars.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个人都说你把车厢清理干净了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们做到了。

sentences.en: We got the cars clean, but we also fixed them.
sentences.zh: 我们把车厢弄干净了，但我们也修好了它们。

sentences.en: The Clean Train became sort of symbolic of the fact that the thing worked.
sentences.zh: 清洁列车在某种程度上成为这套系统行之有效的象征。

sentences.en: And here's the difference between you and me and David Gunn.
sentences.zh: 这就是你、我和大卫·冈恩的区别。

sentences.en: When we see graffiti, we think about it in terms of aesthetics.
sentences.zh: 当我们看到涂鸦时，我们会从美学的角度去思考。

sentences.en: We may like it or hate it, but we're reacting to it visually.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会喜欢它或讨厌它，但我们在视觉上做出反应。

sentences.en: David Gunn looks right past all of those wild-style letters and sees a transit system not doing its job.
sentences.zh: 大卫·冈恩直接无视所有那些狂野风格的字母，看到的是一个没有尽到职责的交通系统。

sentences.en: You see graffiti, you got bad maintenance.
sentences.zh: 你看到了涂鸦，就说明你遇到了糟糕的维护。

sentences.en: Because having equipment clean is part of maintenance.
sentences.zh: 因为保持设备清洁是维护工作的一部分。

sentences.en: For decades, people in charge treated subway graffiti like it was a sanitation problem.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，负责人一直把地铁涂鸦当作卫生问题来处理。

sentences.en: Gunn says that's all wrong.
sentences.zh: 冈恩说这全错了。

sentences.en: It wasn't just a sanitation problem.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个卫生问题。

sentences.en: It was something else entirely.
sentences.zh: 这是完全另外一回事。

sentences.en: Gunn says the root of the problem was MTA's deferred maintenance program.
sentences.zh: 冈恩表示，问题的根源在于MTA的延期维护项目。

sentences.en: In the 70s, New York City was broke.
sentences.zh: 在70年代，纽约市破产了。

sentences.en: And the city pays for a big chunk of the transit authority's operating budget.
sentences.zh: 而城市承担了交通局运营预算很大一部分。

sentences.en: So they asked the MTA to reduce its budget because fewer people were riding the subways.
sentences.zh: 所以他们要求MTA削减预算，因为乘地铁的人变少了。

sentences.en: The MTA made the worst decision.
sentences.zh: MTA做出了最糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: They cut back on the things that kept the subways running.
sentences.zh: 他们削减了维持地铁运行的各项开支。

sentences.en: Routine inspections, replacing parts, even subway mechanics.
sentences.zh: 例行检查、更换零部件，甚至地铁机械师。

sentences.en: And what you expect to happen, happened.
sentences.zh: 而你预料会发生的事情，果然发生了。

sentences.en: The subway deteriorated.
sentences.zh: 地铁系统恶化了。

sentences.en: Breakdowns tripled.
sentences.zh: 故障率增加了两倍。

sentences.en: Trains derailed nearly every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 列车几乎每两周就会脱轨一次。

sentences.en: And get this.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此。

sentences.en: In 1981, there were 1,800 subway car fires.
sentences.zh: 在1981年，发生了1800起地铁车厢火灾。

sentences.en: Ridership should go down when there's 1,800 fires.
sentences.zh: 当发生1800起火灾时，客流量理应下降。

sentences.en: No wonder David Gunn called running the MTA a suicide mission.
sentences.zh: 难怪大卫·冈恩把运营MTA称为自杀任务。

sentences.en: Still, he took it on.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是接受了挑战。

sentences.en: First, he hired 1,500 non-union managers and increased repair staff.
sentences.zh: 首先，他雇用了1500名非工会经理，并增加了维修人员。

sentences.en: He rebuilt thousands of cars.
sentences.zh: 他重建了数千辆车厢。

sentences.en: They had new control cases, rebuild trucks, new motors, air compressors, motor alternators.
sentences.zh: 他们有了新的控制箱、重建的转向架、新的马达、空气压缩机、电动机组。

sentences.en: The whole nine yards.
sentences.zh: 应有尽有。

sentences.en: Here's the thing about maintenance.
sentences.zh: 关于维护，情况是这样的。

sentences.en: It's not sexy.
sentences.zh: 它并不性感。

sentences.en: It takes years to see improvements.
sentences.zh: 需要数年时间才能看到改善。

sentences.en: Gunn knew people needed to see something now.
sentences.zh: 冈恩知道人们需要立刻看到成效。

sentences.en: Or in this case, not see something.
sentences.zh: 或者在这种情况下，是看不到某些东西。

sentences.en: My approach was to drive the bastards out and to clean up the mess they'd made and fix the equipment.
sentences.zh: 我的方法是将这群混蛋赶出去，清理他们制造的混乱，并修理设备。

sentences.en: And we gradually drove the little bastards into a corner.
sentences.zh: 我们逐渐把这群小混蛋逼到了死角。

sentences.en: By little bastards, if it's not obvious, Gunn meant everyone vandalizing the trains.
sentences.zh: 如果还不明显的话，冈恩所说的小混蛋指的是所有破坏列车的人。

sentences.en: And here's how he did it.
sentences.zh: 他是这样做的。

sentences.en: He figured out a way to do it systemically, line by line.
sentences.zh: 他想出了一种按系统、按线路逐步解决的方法。

sentences.en: Again, that's artist Caleb Nealon.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，那是艺术家卡勒布·尼龙。

sentences.en: Like the A line, or the 1 line, or the 2 line.
sentences.zh: 就像A线，或者1号线，或者2号线。

sentences.en: Taking the 7 line off the map for graffiti writers.
sentences.zh: 将7号线从涂鸦者的地图上划掉。

sentences.en: While they were fixing it, they didn't allow any graffiti on it.
sentences.zh: 在他们修复期间，不允许任何涂鸦出现在上面。

sentences.en: Zero.
sentences.zh: 零容忍。

sentences.en: And if graffiti artists bombed a train car.
sentences.zh: 如果涂鸦艺术家对一辆列车喷涂。

sentences.en: Bombed, in this case, means covering the outside of the train with graffiti.
sentences.zh: 在这里，“轰炸”是指用涂鸦覆盖列车外部。

sentences.en: If an artist managed that.
sentences.zh: 如果某个艺术家真的做到了这一点。

sentences.en: The MTA pulled it from the system.
sentences.zh: MTA就会将该车从系统中撤出。

sentences.en: Even during rush hour.
sentences.zh: 即使在交通高峰期也一样。

sentences.en: It was tough going at firSt.
sentences.zh: 一开始非常艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, we had one day I ended up pulling 500 cars out of service.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一天我最终撤下了500辆处于运营状态的车厢。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而它确实管用了。

sentences.en: And people knew it because they could see it.
sentences.zh: 人们之所以知道，是因为他们亲眼所见。

sentences.en: Gunn achieved the impossible.
sentences.zh: 甘恩完成了不可能的任务。

sentences.en: He got rid of graffiti on New York City's subways.
sentences.zh: 他清除了纽约市地铁上的涂鸦。

sentences.en: There is even an official date.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一个确切的日期。

sentences.en: People remember VE and VJ Day.
sentences.zh: 人们还记得欧战胜利纪念日和对日战争胜利纪念日。

sentences.en: You know, this was like their greatest generation moment for the people who ran the subway system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对运营地铁系统的人来说，这就像是他们的“最伟大的一代”的高光时刻。

sentences.en: This was, you know, this was the time when they were declaring victory.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他们宣布胜利的时刻。

sentences.en: The Transit Authority held a ceremony that day.
sentences.zh: 运输出局当天举行了一个仪式。

sentences.en: It was up at 207th Street Shop.
sentences.zh: 地点在207街车间。

sentences.en: That's at the end of the A train.
sentences.zh: 那是在A线地铁的终点站。

sentences.en: All of the MTA brass and a lot of employees were there.
sentences.zh: 所有大都会北方铁路的高层和许多员工都在场。

sentences.en: Amir Ed Koch was there, too.
sentences.zh: 时任市长郭克也出席了。

sentences.en: Privately, I bet he never thought he'd see you that day.
sentences.zh: 私下里，我敢说他从没想过那天会见到你。

sentences.en: And he said I was right.
sentences.zh: 他说我是对的。

sentences.en: They even made commemorative t-shirts.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至制作了纪念T恤。

sentences.en: They were red, and they had the old New York City Transit Authority logo on them.
sentences.zh: 它们是红色的，上面印有旧版纽约市运输局的标志。

sentences.en: And down below it had graffiti-free in the date, you know, because I wore it for a year.
sentences.zh: 下面写着“无涂鸦”以及日期，你知道的，因为我穿了一整年。

sentences.en: It's funny now to ride the subway and imagine that there ever was so much graffiti.
sentences.zh: 现在坐地铁时，很难想象曾经有过那么多涂鸦。

sentences.en: I mean, I've lived in New York for almost 10 years now, and no graffiti-covered subway has ever pulled up to my stop.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在纽约住了快十年了，从来没有一辆沾满涂鸦的地铁开到我的站台。

sentences.en: I always wondered, where did the graffiti go?
sentences.zh: 我总是纳闷，涂鸦都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: I thought the answer might be more complex.
sentences.zh: 我以为答案可能会更复杂。

sentences.en: But this time, for once, the answer is simple.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，破天荒地，答案很简单。

sentences.en: You can point to a man, David Gunn.
sentences.zh: 你可以归功于一个人，大卫·甘恩。

sentences.en: David Gunn, who I think, like a lot of New Yorkers, was this, you know, white knight coming in to fix the subway system.
sentences.zh: 大卫·甘恩，我认为他和许多纽约人一样，就像是一个来拯救地铁系统的白衣骑士。

sentences.en: And, you know, to graffiti writers, he was this Darth Vader character.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在涂鸦创作者眼里，他就像个黑武士达斯·维达。

sentences.en: And, you know, took away their fun, and ultimately was better at taking away their fun than they were at sustaining it.
sentences.zh: 剥夺了他们的乐趣，归根结底，他剥夺他们乐趣的能力，比他们维持乐趣的能力还要强。

sentences.en: May 12, 1989, the day Subway Graffiti died.
sentences.zh: 1989年5月12日，地铁涂鸦消亡的日子。

sentences.en: Hold up.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: The story's not over.
sentences.zh: 故事还没结束。

sentences.en: Graffiti didn't actually end that day.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦在那天并没有真正终结。

sentences.en: There is still Subway Graffiti, but because of David Gunn's clean train program,
sentences.zh: 现在依然有地铁涂鸦，但由于大卫·甘恩的“清洁列车计划”，

sentences.en: it's almost become impossible for us on the outside to see.
sentences.zh: 我们这些局外人几乎不可能看到了。

sentences.en: It almost never leaves the train yards.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎从不驶出列车车场。

sentences.en: MTA crews are on patrol there, constantly looking for graffiti and hosing it off with these crazy solvents if they see any.
sentences.zh: MTA的工作人员在那里巡逻，时刻搜寻涂鸦，一旦发现就用那些疯狂的溶剂冲洗掉。

sentences.en: And they see it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们确实能看到。

sentences.en: An international gallery of it, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这里简直是个国际涂鸦画廊。

sentences.en: So the kid from Munich would go paint subways in Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以慕尼黑的小伙子会去巴黎画地铁。

sentences.en: The kid in, you know, Paris would go paint subways in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，巴黎的小伙子会去阿姆斯特丹画地铁。

sentences.en: Graffiti writers today are kind of like stamp collectors,
sentences.zh: 如今的涂鸦创作者有点像集邮爱好者，

sentences.en: hitting the Berlin's Ubon, the Paris Metro, and the London Tube to put into their album.
sentences.zh: 他们打卡柏林地铁、巴黎地铁和伦敦地铁，把它们收录进自己的相册里。

sentences.en: Collections are judged by two things, size and value.
sentences.zh: 收藏品的评判标准有两个：规模和价值。

sentences.en: The Subway Graffiti completist would have to hit 190 systems in 54 countries.
sentences.zh: 追求完美的地铁涂鸦发烧友必须打卡54个国家的190个地铁系统。

sentences.en: And as for value, there's only one that matters.
sentences.zh: 至于价值，只有一个标准说了算。

sentences.en: There's a real way of thinking in graffiti, which I don't think is entirely wrong,
sentences.zh: 涂鸦界有一种根深蒂固的想法，我觉得这并非完全错误，

sentences.en: which says you're not a real writer until you've got your piece on a New York subway.
sentences.zh: 那就是：除非你的作品上了纽约地铁，否则你就不算是个真正的涂鸦写手。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the holy grail of all trains, you know?
sentences.zh: 这有点像所有火车心中的圣杯，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Right now, spray painting a New York subway car is a felony.
sentences.zh: 现在，在纽约地铁车厢上喷漆属于重罪。

sentences.en: If painters get caught, it could mean jail time and thousands of dollars in fines.
sentences.zh: 如果画家被抓住，可能面临牢狱之灾和数千美元的罚款。

sentences.en: Graffiti artists have to ask themselves,
sentences.zh: 涂鸦艺术家们不得不自问：

sentences.en: is this worth it?
sentences.zh: 这值得吗？

sentences.en: I'm pretty nervous talking on the microphone right now, even about it,
sentences.zh: 我现在对着麦克风说话时挺紧张的，哪怕只是谈论这件事，

sentences.en: because, you know, it's not really something that people are like,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，这并不是那种会让人觉得“太棒了，你在画地铁，真不错，谢谢你这么做”的事。

sentences.en: great, you're painting the subway, that's very nice, thank you for doing that.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's the total opposite, you know?
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，你知道吗？

sentences.en: This is Joe, or at least that's what he wanted me to call him.
sentences.zh: 这是乔，至少他希望我这么叫他。

sentences.en: Joe is a graffiti artist from South Africa.
sentences.zh: 乔是一位来自南非的涂鸦艺术家。

sentences.en: He hits trains in countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 他在世界各地的国家喷涂列车。

sentences.en: He didn't want to say if he was going to hit New York.
sentences.zh: 他不愿意透露他是否会去纽约。

sentences.en: You can't say.
sentences.zh: 你不能说。

sentences.en: I can't say.
sentences.zh: 我不能说。

sentences.en: No, no, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我不是那个意思。

sentences.en: We distorted Joe's voice to protect his identity.
sentences.zh: 我们对乔的声音进行了变声处理以保护他的身份。

sentences.en: That's the only way that he would agree to talk to us.
sentences.zh: 这是他唯一愿意与我们交谈的方式。

sentences.en: Joe's never been caught, but it's been close.
sentences.zh: 乔从未被抓过，但好几次险些落网。

sentences.en: I've looked, seen a flashlight,
sentences.zh: 我看到过手电筒的光，

sentences.en: and turned around to tell the guy that someone is coming for us.
sentences.zh: 然后转身告诉同伴有人朝我们来了。

sentences.en: And when I've turned around, he's already, like, running.
sentences.zh: 当我转过身时，他已经跑了。

sentences.en: We actually caught a couple of guys from Australia just last week
sentences.zh: 就在上周，我们确实抓住了几个来自澳大利亚的家伙，

sentences.en: who are trying to breach our security and go into a yard.
sentences.zh: 他们试图突破我们的安保防线潜入车场。

sentences.en: And now, Vincent Di Marino.
sentences.zh: 现在出场的是文森特·迪马里诺。

sentences.en: He's the vice president of security for the MTA and New York City Transit.
sentences.zh: 他是MTA和纽约市运输局的安全副总裁。

sentences.en: He sees guys from all over the world in New York's train yards.
sentences.zh: 他在纽约的车场里见过来自世界各地的人。

sentences.en: Di Marino didn't have hard numbers of who gets caught from where in the yards.
sentences.zh: 迪马里诺没有掌握具体在车场被捕的人都来自哪里的确切数据。

sentences.en: But when a train gets hit in New York,
sentences.zh: 但每当纽约的列车遭到涂鸦袭击时，

sentences.en: the graffiti artist is more likely to be from, say, Spain or France,
sentences.zh: 涂鸦艺术家更有可能来自西班牙或法国等地，

sentences.en: not from New York.
sentences.zh: 而不是来自纽约。

sentences.en: Some have put the ratio at something like 80-20.
sentences.zh: 有人估计这一比例大约是80比20。

sentences.en: The international folks, it's cost them a lot of money to do.
sentences.zh: 这些国际友人为此花费了大量金钱。

sentences.en: You know, if I was to get on a plane, I'd go somewhere and sit on a beach.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我要坐飞机，我会找个地方在海滩上坐着。

sentences.en: I wouldn't buy an airplane ticket to go commit a crime in a train yard.
sentences.zh: 我不会买机票去列车车场犯罪。

sentences.en: Graffiti artists say that's part of the draw.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦艺术家说，这就是吸引力的一部分。

sentences.en: It's a rush to break the law.
sentences.zh: 打破法律会带来一种刺激感。

sentences.en: Nah, I want to get over this f***ing fence.
sentences.zh: 不，我要翻过这该死的栅栏。

sentences.en: It's hard to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 这很难抗拒。

sentences.en: It's exciting at first, you know, when you go inside to the yard.
sentences.zh: 刚开始进入车场时，那种感觉非常刺激，你知道的。

sentences.en: And you stand on the floor, you're not on the platform,
sentences.zh: 当你站在地面上而不是站台上时，

sentences.en: and you see how big this train really is.
sentences.zh: 你就会发现这列火车实际上有多大。

sentences.en: I mean, when you're on the platform, a train's a train.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你在站台上时，火车就是列火车。

sentences.en: And when you're on the floor next to it, it's like an iron beast, you know?
sentences.zh: 但当你站在它旁边的地面上时，它就像一头铁血野兽，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Gotta love it.
sentences.zh: 不得不爱。

sentences.en: It's intoxicating.
sentences.zh: 太让人着迷了。

sentences.en: The smell and the sound is so much more intense because you're already, like, super nervous.
sentences.zh: 由于你本来就已经超级紧张，气味和声音会变得更加强烈。

sentences.en: Look what's coming at you.
sentences.zh: 看看朝你驶来的是什么。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: There's not much that could beat that feeling.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能比得上那种感觉。

sentences.en: It's, like, better than sex, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像，比做爱还爽，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, better than money, better than anything.
sentences.zh: 就像，比金钱更好，比任何东西都好。

sentences.en: It's, like, that's why people do it.
sentences.zh: 就像，这就是人们这么做原因。

sentences.en: That's why someone would risk their career and their life to press the button on a spray can
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有人会冒着毁掉职业生涯和生命的风险，去按下喷漆罐的喷头，

sentences.en: and see if you put colors on a train, you know?
sentences.zh: 看看能否给火车添上色彩，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I see the Europeans doing it.
sentences.zh: 我看到欧洲人在这么做。

sentences.en: So I'm like, why New York?
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，为什么不选纽约？

sentences.en: Dudes ain't doing it.
sentences.zh: 本地小伙子们都不干了。

sentences.en: Like, this is where it's from.
sentences.zh: 听着，这就是它的发源地。

sentences.en: This is where it was built at.
sentences.zh: 这就是它诞生的文化背景。

sentences.en: Like, I say, you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Let me bring the trains back.
sentences.zh: 让我把这些列车带回过去的模样。

sentences.en: This is CT.
sentences.zh: 我是CT。

sentences.en: I spell it C-E-T-E, and then I have a two-letter, C-T.
sentences.zh: 我拼写为C-E-T-E，然后我有一个两个字母的缩写，C-T。

sentences.en: The same thing means clean trains, if people don't get it.
sentences.zh: 如果人们不明白的话，它的意思就是清洁列车。

sentences.en: CT tells me he always feels like an old soul.
sentences.zh: CT告诉我，他觉得自己总有一种老派的灵魂。

sentences.en: But I'd call him a romantic.
sentences.zh: 但我称他为浪漫主义者。

sentences.en: I seen it on the trains, and I seen Subway R, and I'm like, damn, I missed this time.
sentences.zh: 我在火车上见过，也在R线地铁上见过，当时我想，操，我错过了那个时代。

sentences.en: CT bombed not one, but two trains this year.
sentences.zh: CT今年不仅涂了一列，而是涂了两列火车。

sentences.en: The first was the R train.
sentences.zh: 第一列是R线地铁。

sentences.en: It was a spy versus spy theme.
sentences.zh: 主题是间谍对间谍。

sentences.en: It took about 11 cans and an hour to paint, but days and days of preparation.
sentences.zh: 画完大约用了11罐喷漆和一个小时，但前期准备花了整整好几天。

sentences.en: I studied these lines.
sentences.zh: 我研究了这些线路。

sentences.en: I studied the times.
sentences.zh: 我研究了时间表。

sentences.en: I even studied down to the workers, because if you could find a lazy worker one day,
sentences.zh: 我甚至把工人的情况都研究透了，因为如果你能发现某个偷懒的工人，

sentences.en: hey, you could do a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你就能干成很多事。

sentences.en: And this MTA, they have a lot of lazy workers.
sentences.zh: 而MTA这里，有很多偷懒的工人。

sentences.en: The second train they hit was a B train, this time with a Pink Panther theme.
sentences.zh: 他们袭击的第二列车是B线地铁，这次的主题是粉红豹。

sentences.en: We had the whole day planned like a recon mission.
sentences.zh: 我们像执行侦察任务一样计划了整整一天。

sentences.en: And here's what ties CT and David Gunn together.
sentences.zh: 这就是将CT和大卫·甘恩联系在一起的地方。

sentences.en: Both men have spent a lot of time scrutinizing the weak points in the MTA system.
sentences.zh: 这两个人都花了很多时间仔细研究MTA系统的薄弱环节。

sentences.en: CT dreams of bringing back New York's Subway graffiti.
sentences.zh: CT梦想着让纽约的地铁涂鸦卷土重来。

sentences.en: But the number of hits are rapidly declining.
sentences.zh: 但被袭击的次数正在急剧下降。

sentences.en: In 2007, there were 75-yard hits.
sentences.zh: 在2007年，车场袭击事件有75起。

sentences.en: So far this year, only nine.
sentences.zh: 而今年到目前为止，只有9起。

sentences.en: The MTA's police force can take some credit for those numbers, but there is another factor.
sentences.zh: MTA的警察部队对这些数字功不可没，但还有另一个因素。

sentences.en: I find it hard to think of graffiti writers who are much under 25.
sentences.zh: 我发现很难想象还有多少25岁以下的涂鸦创作者。

sentences.en: And a lot of the most active people that I know are in their 40s, honestly.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我认识的许多最活跃的人都已经40多岁了。

sentences.en: Graffiti as an art form may just age out at some point.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦作为一种艺术形式，可能在某个时候会自然消亡。

sentences.en: And if Subway graffiti did die out, how would we even know?
sentences.zh: 如果地铁涂鸦真的消亡了，我们又怎么会知道呢？

sentences.en: The artists know that their work will never be seen by the public at large.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们知道，他们的作品永远不会被大众所看到。

sentences.en: They break into the train yard, paint their murals, and immediately after, the Subway cars are scrubbed clean by MTA workers.
sentences.zh: 他们潜入车场，画上壁画，紧接着，地铁车厢就会被MTA的工人擦拭干净。

sentences.en: The art form is totally ephemeral.
sentences.zh: 这种艺术形式是完全转瞬即逝的。

sentences.en: It reminds me of those Tibetan sand mandalas made to disappear.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起那些注定要被抹去的西藏沙曼陀罗。

sentences.en: Pretty much all that keeps that from happening right now is social media.
sentences.zh: 目前几乎只有社交媒体在阻止这一切彻底发生。

sentences.en: There are invitation-only Instagram accounts where Subway bombers post their work before it disappears.
sentences.zh: 有些仅限受邀加入的Instagram账号，地铁涂鸦客们会在作品消失前把它发到上面。

sentences.en: Those painted trains that crossed our movie screens on countless establishing shots of dirty New York City in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 那些在20世纪70年代描绘脏乱纽约市的无数电影镜头中穿梭的彩绘列车，

sentences.en: They're just a little square on your smartphone now.
sentences.zh: 如今只成了你智能手机上的一个小方块。

sentences.en: And by the time you see them, they're already gone.
sentences.zh: 而当你看到它们时，它们已经消失了。

sentences.en: My love is the trains.
sentences.zh: 我爱的是列车。

sentences.en: There's always going to be trains until the casket drops.
sentences.zh: 只要人还没入棺材，就总会有列车存在。

sentences.en: There's always going to be trains.
sentences.zh: 总会有列车存在。

sentences.en: And, um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，是的。

sentences.en: That's about it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 差不多就是这样，对。

sentences.en: Let's roll.
sentences.zh: 我们出发吧。

sentences.en: Until the casket drops, or until the NYPD anti-graffiti unit called the Vandal Squad catches up to you.
sentences.zh: 直到棺材板合上，或者直到纽约警察局的反涂鸦部门——“破坏小组”抓到你为止。

sentences.en: Which is what happened to CT.
sentences.zh: 这就是CT的遭遇。

sentences.en: He was arrested and charged with more than 180 misdemeanor counts for things like
sentences.zh: 他被捕并被控犯有180多项轻罪，罪名包括

sentences.en: possession of a graffiti instrument and intention to damage property, along with some felony charges.
sentences.zh: 持有涂鸦工具和意图损坏财产，此外还有一些重罪指控。

sentences.en: He took a plea deal, agreed to pay nearly $19,000 in restitution charges, and is now on probation.
sentences.zh: 他接受了认罪协议，同意支付近19,000美元的赔偿金，目前正处于缓刑期。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Ann Hepperman, with help from Julia Barton,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由安·海佩曼制作，朱莉娅·巴顿提供帮助，

sentences.en: Roby Flores, Sam Greenspan, Katie Mingle, Avery Truffelman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 罗比·弗洛雷斯、萨姆·格林斯潘、凯蒂·明格尔、艾弗里·特鲁费尔曼，以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco, and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 地方公共广播电台 KALW 的一个项目，在 ArcSign 的办公室制作，

sentences.en: the coolest architecture firm in beautiful Graffiti Adept, downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的“涂鸦达人”最酷的建筑事务所。

sentences.en: If you like fun, you can keep up with this show and all the people who make this show
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢有趣的内容，可以在

sentences.en: at Facebook, Twitter, and Tumblr.
sentences.zh: Facebook、Twitter和Tumblr上关注本节目以及所有制作人员。

sentences.en: But if you want to see the Spy vs. Spy subway car, it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想看看《间谍对间谍》的地铁车厢，那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: You have to go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你必须访问 99pi.org。

sentences.en: This is the last stop on this train.
sentences.zh: 这是这趟列车的最后一站。

sentences.en: Everyone please leave the MTA New York...
sentences.zh: 请大家离开MTA纽约...

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
